findings.evidence: SafeProviderPath checks Path.IsPathRooted and the drive-letter form before trimming. A provider scalar such as ` C:\Users\Admin\private\secret.cs` therefore passes the initial checks, is trimmed to `C:/Users/Admin/private/secret.cs`, and is retained as a known path. A read-only .NET path check reproduced that the pre-trim value is not rooted while the post-trim value resolves to `C:\Users\Admin\private\secret.cs`. A malformed provider row can consequently place the absolute host path in ProviderCandidateOutcome and the coordinator warning log. Existing matrices cover unpadded drive, UNC, POSIX-rooted, traversal, control-character, empty-segment, and oversize inputs but not boundary-whitespace drive paths.
findings.correction_outcome: Observe regression RED for leading/trailing-whitespace rooted inputs, then make rooted, drive, segment, and control validation operate on one normalized candidate or reject boundary whitespace outright. Prove the raw value and every host fragment are absent from the provider result, captured logs, durable outcome, API response, and UI.

findings.evidence: ParsePythonRequirements rejects only leading hyphen, URL, and environment-marker forms, then scans a valid package-name prefix without validating the remainder of the line. Invalid or ambiguous text such as `django???` therefore produces the exact catalog coordinate `python:django` and a High-confidence Django fact even though it is not a supported literal requirement. Current tests cover includes, URLs, editable entries, and markers but not invalid trailing syntax.
findings.correction_outcome: Add observed RED cases for invalid trailing syntax and require a closed full-line literal-requirement grammar before matching the package coordinate. Unsupported or malformed lines must create no framework fact and must retain only the bounded closed audit outcome while valid independent evidence continues.

findings.evidence: SelectApplicable computes manifestCount only from PackageEvidence that already matched the framework catalog. With two successfully parsed same-root NuGet project manifests where one declares a catalog-matched framework and the other contains only valid unmatched declarations, only the matched project enters winningScope. manifestCount is one, so the matched framework is assigned even though the Code Unit's same-ecosystem project scope is ambiguous. The existing ambiguity test uses two catalog-matched projects and does not exercise the matched-plus-unmatched case.
findings.correction_outcome: Observe RED for a matched plus valid-unmatched same-root project pair, retain supported direct-manifest scope identities independently from catalog-matched evidence, and suppress all same-ecosystem facts at an ambiguous winning root with one bounded ambiguity audit outcome. Preserve independent colocated ecosystems and deeper unambiguous scopes.
